claim: MRSC global tables can now be created in any combination of three of the 15 supported Regions, including Regions on different continents. The announcement added five Regions: Canada (Central), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Spain), Asia Pacific (Mumbai) and Asia Pacific (Singapore).
question: Which Regions can an MRSC global table use, and what did the late-2026 expansion add?

values.display: any combination of three of these Regions
values.spoken: any three of the supported Regions

values.display: total number of supported Regions to 15

qualifiers.condition: the full Region list is on the global tables guide page

evidence.quote: MRSC global tables are available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Spain), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Singapore). An MRSC global table can include replicas from any combination of three of these Regions, including Regions on different continents.
You can now create an MRSC global table in any three-Region configuration across the 15 supported AWS Regions, configured with either three replicas or two replicas and one witness Region.

note: Announced 2026-09-23 (What's New), after the 2026-07-15 cutoff: label 'not examinable yet'. The guide page now lists 15 Regions; older material lists fewer Regions and may say MRSC replicas cannot span continents.

claim: DynamoDB global tables can replicate across multiple AWS accounts and Regions, with each replica in a distinct account for account-level fault isolation and separate security and governance controls. Older material describes global tables as same-account only.
question: Can DynamoDB global table replicas live in different AWS accounts, and since when?

values.display: across multiple AWS Regions and multiple AWS accounts
Each replica table resides in a distinct AWS account

evidence.quote: Multi-account global tables automatically replicate your DynamoDB table data across multiple AWS Regions and multiple AWS accounts to improve resiliency, isolate workloads at the account level, and apply distinct security and governance controls. Each replica table resides in a distinct AWS account, enabling fault isolation at both the Region and account level.

This capability allows you to strengthen fault tolerance and helps ensure applications remain highly available even during account-level disruptions, while allowing customers to align data placement with organizational and security requirements.

note: Announced 2026-02-03 (What's New); before the 2026-07-15 cutoff, so examinable. Needs resource-based policies that grant the global tables service principal.
